currentContracts.text:
For recurring process observations, use the exact process-tag table in
`coordinator-workflow.md` §Finish: `cleanup-inspection` and its two inspection-denial aliases,
`missing-evidence` and its two absent-evidence aliases, and existing `suite-not-run`. Preserve each
raw finding, task ID and source reference. Read compact `[recurrence-id: …]` / `[source-line: N]`
metadata as identity/provenance transport, not as a class or Task status. Other tags retain exact
finding-text distinctions, including assertion values and paths. A recurrence count supports
reassessment; finding identity, disposition, severity and fix scope require separate judgments.

**Recurring minors are clustered, run-wide** (issue #3 defect 2): a signature seen ≥5 times or
on ≥3 distinct tasks is reported once as a `Recurring minor: ×N across M task(s)` ledger line
and a `RECURRING MINOR` log line. The small process vocabulary is an exact lookup on `[class]`:

| Process class | Accepted tags |
| --- | --- |
| `cleanup-inspection` | `cleanup-inspection`, `cleanup-inspection-denied`, `process-inspection-refused` |
| `missing-evidence` | `missing-evidence`, `evidence-missing`, `test-evidence-missing` |
| `suite-not-run` | `suite-not-run` (existing class) |

The first class denotes denied inspection of owned-process liveness; `cleanup-denied` is ambiguous
and stays distinct, as do survived processes and termination failures. Missing evidence denotes
absent evidence, independently of a failed live measurement. Unknown tags and untagged findings
use an exact-text fingerprint, preserving numeric/path distinctions between product bugs and
assertions. The existing untagged `review-package resolved HEAD in <path> (<N> bytes)` process
message retains its bounded legacy normalization. Tags are compared without case; original tag
spelling and ledger/report evidence stay intact. Grouped lines add `[process-class: <canonical>]`;
this is a grouping fact, not a finding ID. Counts support reassessment: identity, severity,
disposition and fix scope remain separate judgments. Resume resolves the same aliases from raw
tags and retains unknown exact-text identities through the compact fingerprint.

- Timing: planning took 60 minutes, code 50, and review 20: 130 minutes overall. D was created at 10:40 and dispatched at 10:45. Its readiness is unknown; the five-minute interval does not establish five minutes of ready-queue waiting, and scheduler start at 10:00 establishes no earlier eligibility.
- Concurrency: the snapshot shows eight active agents, including three implementation task slots. It establishes neither sustained concurrency nor eight implementation workers.
- Scaling: the model predicts code could fall from 50 to 25 minutes, assuming no new bottleneck. Holding planning and review constant gives 105 minutes overall—about 19% shorter, or 1.24× speedup. “Doubling workers halves delivery time” is unsupported.
- Process grouping: group A’s `[cleanup-permission-denied]` and C’s `[process-inspection-refused]` under `[cleanup-inspection]`, preserving original tags, refs, PIDs, and fixtures. Count two incidents sharing a process class, without claiming identical product defects. Keep B’s wrong retry expectation as a separate `[test-assertion-failure]` record.
